Every one of the 38 ranked models found a worthwhile risk (a risky play at least 0.001 better than the best safe play) in a smaller share of the risk-pays positions than the share of safety-pays positions they played safe: risks found runs from 18.7% to 53.3%, safe right from 59.8% to 97.6%. GNUbg weak, a weak setting of the engine (grey square), is close to even: 67.6% safe right, 66.6% risks found. Above the diagonal, a model succeeds more often when safety pays than when risk pays; the chart compares these two success rates, not how often a model plays risky at all.

A release month is documented for 24 of the 38 ranked models; only those are shown, each at the month of its maker's own dated statement. Makers with models in different months, earliest first: Google 64.5, 66.9, 74.1; Fastino 60.4, 58.8. That is not a consistent increase across the makers shown.

Asked which of two plays is better on the same rollout-confirmed positions, all 8 models chose the safe play more often when the prompt showed each play's computed numbers than from the board alone: the bias (missed minus needless) moves from -22 pp to +92 pp for Jev 1.14.0 and from +46 pp to +56 pp for Claude Opus 5.5 (high). From the board alone, 4 of them (Celeris-1 Decision, Jev 1.14.0, Liquid d1-ultra, Kimi K3.1 Pro (off)) took more needless risks than they missed.

9 models played two or more reasoning settings in the same league. At the highest setting, 9 of the 9 had a lower error rate than at the lowest, and 7 of the 9 a higher risk judgement. GPT-6 Astra, low to high: risk judgement 75.8, 74.7, 74.4; error rate 11.8, 11.1, 8.8.
